# Was the RIKEN Fugaku supercomputer break-in a hack?

**Confirmed.** Yes, by RIKEN's own account: an outside party got into Fugaku's operational network from Nov 10 to 13, installed malicious programs on some servers and took users' files, including private keys. Who did it is not known.

Incident: RIKEN Fugaku supercomputer break-in, Nov 2026. Also reported as the Fugaku hack and the RIKEN supercomputer cyberattack. First published Nov 21, 2026; last updated Nov 21, 2026, 12:12 AM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by RIKEN, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 21, 2026, 12:12 AM ET: **RIKEN says an outsider entered Fugaku through its public status dashboard and took 430 private keys; the machine is offline.** First draft. 4 sources (2 Tier 1), 13 claims (9 Confirmed, 1 Reported, 3 Not established), 6 questions. RIKEN's two notices confirm the break-in, the stolen keys and the user counts. The attacker and any use of the keys elsewhere are not established. Shutdown time follows RIKEN (Nov 14, 4:30 AM Japan time). Privacy check done: no individuals named, no contact details.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Regional. One national research supercomputer in Japan, offline since Nov 14. Up to 4,222 Fugaku users and 375 RIKYU users are affected, and stolen keys could reach other research computers.
- Who is affected: Registered users of Fugaku and RIKYU, who are researchers, and researchers waiting for time on the machine. Their contact details and any private keys stored on Fugaku were involved.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 430 | Private keys taken | 233 with no passphrase |
| 4,222 | Fugaku users, up to | Plus 375 RIKYU users |
| Nov 14 | Fugaku taken offline | 4:30 AM Japan time |

### Known so far

- An outside party got into Fugaku's operational network between Nov 10 and 13, through the public status dashboard.
- Malicious programs were installed on some servers.
- 430 private keys for outside systems were taken, 233 of them without a passphrase.
- Fugaku was suspended on Nov 14 and has no restart date.

### Not known yet

- Who was behind it.
- Whether the stolen keys were used to break into other organizations.
- The exact method used to get past the dashboard.
- When Fugaku will return to service.

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of this page's first draft.

- Who was behind it, or any claim of responsibility.
- The exact method used to get past the dashboard.
- A confirmed break-in at another organization using a stolen key.
- A date for Fugaku's return to service.
- Whether research data or other people's personal information was taken. RIKEN said on Nov 16 it had no evidence; we have not seen a later update.
- RIKEN's statement of the root cause. The second notice says an investigative committee with outside experts will be set up.
